title: The Book of the Dead
objective: After this level you can explain what the Book of the Dead was for.
summary: The Book of the Dead was a papyrus roll of spells to protect the dead. It grew from the royal Pyramid Texts and the Coffin Texts and was bought for burials.

cards.headline: The Book of the Dead wasn’t a book, and Egyptians didn’t call it that.
cards.body: It was a roll of spells: a guidebook and protection kit for the hardest journey an Egyptian expected to make.

cards.headline: Spells for the road
cards.body: Its Egyptian title was “The Chapters of Coming Forth by Day.” It collected spells placed in tombs to protect and help the dead; about 200 are known. Some kept you from losing your head or your heart. Others protected you from snakes, crocodiles and insects along the way. Spell 125 covered the judgment before Osiris from Level 36. An exam, with the answers packed in the luggage.

cards.headline: Standard or deluxe?
cards.body: Scribes copied the spells onto rolls of papyrus, often colorfully illustrated, and sold them for burials. No papyrus contains every spell. You could buy a ready-made copy with blank spaces for your name, or pay more and probably choose your own spells. On papyrus, the spells reached far more people than ever before, though a fine illustrated copy was expensive. Afterlife insurance came in standard and deluxe.

questions.prompt: What was the Egyptian Book of the Dead?

options.label: A list of everyone buried in a cemetery
options.rationale: It held spells, not names of the buried.

options.label: A collection of spells to protect and help the dead
A history of Egypt’s kings
options.rationale: That would be a king list.

options.label: A handbook for embalmers
options.rationale: It was for the dead themselves.

questions.explanation: It was a collection of spells placed in tombs to protect and help the dead in the afterlife.

questions.prompt: Why could far more Egyptians own afterlife spells once they were written on papyrus?

options.label: Papyrus rolls could be bought, unlike pyramid walls
The government handed them out free
options.rationale: Copies were sold, and fine ones were expensive.

options.label: The spells became shorter and easier to memorize
Only kings were allowed to die
options.rationale: Everyone died; the question was who had spells.

questions.explanation: Pyramid Texts were for kings and Coffin Texts for officials and nobles; papyrus copies were sold to anyone who could pay.

questions.prompt: Egypt’s oldest afterlife spells, the Pyramid Texts, were written in which of Level 1’s great kingdoms?

options.label: The Middle Kingdom
options.rationale: That was the age of the Coffin Texts.

options.label: The New Kingdom
options.rationale: That was the age of papyrus rolls.

questions.explanation: The Pyramid Texts were written inside Old Kingdom pyramids, the age of the great pyramids.
